title: Artificial Intelligence
subtitle: A Guide for Thinking Humans
pitch: A complexity scientist explains how AI really works and argues that machines still lack understanding, the 'barrier of meaning'.

chapters.g: Mitchell describes a Google meeting where her mentor Douglas Hofstadter said he was terrified, and why she felt differently.
The birth of AI in the 1950s and its early big promises.

chapters.t: Neural Networks and the Ascent of Machine Learning
chapters.g: How neural networks work and why they came back.
The deep learning boom and its hype.
What it means for a machine to 'see' an image.
The networks and the dataset behind the vision revolution.

chapters.t: A Closer Look at Machines That Learn
chapters.g: What these systems really learn, including shortcuts and brittleness.
Bias, adversarial examples, and what it takes to trust AI.
Reinforcement learning, explained with a robot dog.
Why success in games does not easily transfer to the real world.

Part IV: Artificial Intelligence Meets Natural Language

chapters.g: Question answering and reading comprehension tests.

chapters.g: What understanding is, and why machines may lack it.
chapters.part: Part V: The Barrier of Meaning

chapters.t: Knowledge, Abstraction, and Analogy in Artificial Intelligence
chapters.g: Analogy making as the core of intelligence, and why it is hard for AI.
chapters.part: Part V: The Barrier of Meaning

chapters.g: Mitchell's answers to big questions, including how far we are from general AI.
chapters.part: Part V: The Barrier of Meaning

ideas: Systems can be brittle and take shortcuts.
Analogy and abstraction are key missing pieces.
Hype can mislead the public and policymakers.

args.a: Human level AI is further away than the hype suggests.
args.c: The book was written before large language models. Many think models since 2020 have narrowed the gap she described.

questions: Has the 'barrier of meaning' been crossed since 2019?
What is the difference between performance and understanding?

quiz.q: What does Mitchell call the key thing AI lacks?
o: The barrier of meaning: real understanding
quiz.w: Part V is titled The Barrier of Meaning.
Her mentor Hofstadter feared AI might cheapen human minds.
